lines: I had a thought once. Left it somewhere safe, probably.
If you find my thought, tell it I was looking useful.
I found a button once. No wall, just ambition.
Where am I going? Usually somewhere nearby, once I remember why.
I tried following my shadow, but it got behind me somehow.
A job sounds useful. I am saving usefulness for the right moment.
A nice stick can be many things if nobody important is watching.
I carried an empty bucket all morning. Very light work. Very confusing.
I once put bread in a chest and called it planning. Nobody argued.
Hello. I was keeping this corner company.
Give the sunny corner room. Odd jobs works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the sunny corner. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
My joke wandered off, but it promised to be funny if it returns.
Odd jobs jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with muddle on them.
I keep a spare joke near the sunny corner. It is not always ready for public use.
Your hat looks like it is thinking harder than you.
I have seen bad guesses with more sense than that.
Careful. Even muddle looks softer than your manners right now.
I can be silly from over here. Over here feels better.
Keep your voice even. I am measuring more than your words.
Some questions are safer when they stand a little farther away.
I remember you! Mostly. You were the not-scary part of the scary bit.
You helped me be me again. I am very attached to being me.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I know your face. Did we meet before or after I stopped groaning?
There was an apple, but not the normal apple kind of day.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember some of it, and I would like to remember less of it.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the village square so hard I jumped before the bell did, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked doors, beds, and hiding places after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
By the bell, the thunder made the whole square flinch. I stayed inside and kept away from windows.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked my hiding spot twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have a safe corner to find.
I checked roofs and fences for sparks, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I carried the bucket after.
My chores can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could near the bell, then made sure no one was still coughing alone.
The smoke is thinner now, but I keep smelling my sleeves to make sure it is really gone.
During a raid, whatever i was doing can wait; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but I still keep looking at the road like it might shout again.
We counted living neighbors before doors, beds, and hiding places. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the bell and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the bell, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble found the door everyone meant to fix tomorrow. It is getting fixed today.
I stayed near the dark between houses and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn made it easier to see who was missing, which is not the same as making it easier.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping both hands free between us and teeth.
We are safe enough, but I still look twice at anything shaped like a monster.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning sand from my sleeves.
I checked doors, beds, and hiding places, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand got in my sleeves, my mouth, and places sand should not know about. No one is missing, though.
A hard wind teaches a nitwit which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough, but every step sounds crunchy and everyone is blinking too much.
Whatever I was doing can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the bell found shelter.
Cold is sneaky. I am checking on anyone who stopped complaining about it.
I am clearing snow out of my shoes and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now. I am keeping close to smoke, soup, and shoveled paths.
We went there, then we came back here. I liked the back here part best.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
I got bonked on the trip. Home is better when fewer things bonk me.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
I thought following meant you were on my side. That was the important bit.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
The boat moved and I did not have to. I liked that part.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
Remember when I followed you? I thought we were going somewhere. We sure did.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
Remember the boat? I sat down and the world moved. Very clever.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
I used it and did not drop it. That is two victories, if you ask me.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
I have not used it. I have practiced looking brave with it, which is almost something.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
I ducked very professionally. You did the scarier part, which was nice.
The horn went bwaa and everyone ran. You ran the useful direction.
You ran toward the loud part. That seemed important and extremely bold.
I was under a table, but I heard useful fighting. Yours, probably.
The village is still here, and I am very attached to that outcome.
You made the raiders stop doing raid things near us. Excellent choice.
I did morale from a safe place. You did the dangerous part.
When the horn sounded, you became part of the answer. I liked that.
That sounded sorry. I am still standing over here for a bit.
I accept the apology, but I am keeping one pocket full of suspicion.
That sounded like the right kind of sorry. I think.
I accept, but I am standing behind this idea of distance for now.
Okay. Try doing the good version of that next time.
I will forgive a bit now and maybe another bit after lunch.
Words received. Suspicion still lightly worn.
Fine. I am putting the apology somewhere safe in my head.
I made it back because I ran exactly the clever amount. No one measures that.
I only ran the wrong way once, maybe twice, and then I found the right door.
I survived by making several choices very quickly and only some of them silly.
The door was exactly where I hoped it was. Eventually.
I came back alive, which is my favorite kind of back.
I was brave for at least three seconds. The rest was very fast walking.
Someone shouted run, and I became excellent at listening.
I made it home and only lost one thought on the way.
Take {gift_item}. I was saving it for a very good reason I forgot.
Here, {gift_item}. It feels like the sort of thing a friend should have.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
See? {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}. I am occasionally brilliant by accident.
Ha! {gift_item} worked. I will be unbearable about this for at least a minute.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.
Oh. Then pretend I said {alternative_gift}. For {gift_subject}, that sounds much wiser.
{gift_item} failed? Strange. Try {alternative_gift}; my second guesses are famous to me.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.
That was advice? I thought we were guessing. Guess {alternative_gift} next.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.
You tried it anyway? Bold. I respect that almost enough to suggest {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.
Mind the sunny corner. What do you need?
Step clear of the sunny corner. What do you need?
Mind the sunny corner; I am listening.
Back to finding odd jobs and stranger thoughts, then.
Back to odd jobs before the work notices I stopped.
I have thought to tend and daylight to spend.
Fine. I was getting tired of being angry anyway.
Fine. I will set this down before it gets heavier.
Fine. I can step back, but do not make me regret it.
I counted, then forgot, then counted again. It should be {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
That is short of the full repair. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
Not enough. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds} to settle this.
No. Even I know this is not fixed.
No. Some damage has to cool before payment matters.
No. Keep {payment_items}; trust is not ready to trade.
